fields.quoted_span:
A housing provider shall not, either before
or after the issuance of a conditional offer, evaluate an applicant based on
any of the following types of criminal records:
fields.note: Each element of the summary traces to the act: the pre-offer inquiry ban and its two exceptions, the barred record types, the post-offer limits, the withdrawal standard, notice, the six factors, the 30-day request and 10-day free response, the fee disclosure, the advertising, drug-test and treatment-records bans, the complaint-only enforcement, the 14-day mediation, the tiered penalties, and the fee return and up-to-$1,000 payment.

fields.note: Lookbacks are 6 years (first degree), 4 years (second or third degree) and 1 year (fourth degree). Listed serious crimes and lifetime-registration crimes carry no time limit. Penalty caps are $1,000, $5,000 and $10,000.

fields.quoted_span:
This act shall take effect on the first day of the
seventh month next following the date of enactment
fields.note: The act was approved June 18, 2021. The first day of the seventh month after that is January 1, 2022.

fields.note: The document shows the act took effect on a fixed date. It says nothing about later amendment or repeal, so 'in_force' as a current status cannot be confirmed from the document alone.

fields.quoted_span:
“Rental dwelling unit” means a dwelling unit offered
for rent by a housing provider for residential purposes,
other than a dwelling unit in an
owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.
fields.note: The definition supports the owner-occupied exemption (four units or fewer) and the coverage summary. The other coverage fields are null, and the document states no conditions for them.

The act is P.L. 2021, c.110 (S250), the Fair Chance in Housing Act. The cited section 46:8-55 is the application-process section. The aliases (46:8-52 to 46:8-64 and the individual sections) match the section headings.
